the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10138 at 15 FR 4241, in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads FEDERAL REGISTER 4241 with the date Tuesday, July 4, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10138, is signed July 3, 1950, and its filing line reads Filed, July 3, 1950. The same page also prints Executive Order 10139, which concerns the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, A. F. of L.; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it states \"I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute.\" It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President \"within thirty days from the date of this order\", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported \"no change, except by agreement, shall be made\" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed \"Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986\" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that \"the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked\"; its No. Subject table lists 10138 with the subject \"Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute\". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10138_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10138_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ba0763e74c.txt, PDF page 1) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed July 3, 1950 by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139, and its title page is dated at Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10136 to 10139 hold the same pages), a Federal Register codification guide for page 4241, and the front matter of the board's report.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report requirement is a deadline, not an end. The board's held report is dated August 11, 1950; that date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The thirty-day period after the report during which no change could be made except by agreement comes from section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the held sources do not show when the President received the report, so no exact end of that period is asserted, and its running out is a spent fact, not an end. (3) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation, and the held-text number search found no other instrument naming the order. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order has no command independent of the board it creates. The bar on interested members, the thirty-day report command and the sentence on unchanged conditions all serve the same board and share the order's end. The sentence on unchanged conditions opens by stating that it is made as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so its force comes from that statute rather than from a separate command of the order.\",\"savings_check\":\"The enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 contains no saving or exception clause, and the ACT record for this pair lists none. The board's investigation, its report and any settlement that followed are completed past events, not continuing commands of this order; the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives it, and no held source shows any continuing effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, its table row matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so it reaches the whole order. The order has no amendment in the held corpus. The dossier lead that Executive Order 10139 cites this order by number is resolved: the held text file for Executive Order 10139 is the same Federal Register page, which prints both orders one after the other; neither order refers to the other, so no change provision is missing.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[{"file_sha256":"9fea503fcb6a0a237442acdd1a35cec14b467e7bcf22422f2e5da8fa80c3b76f","path":"research/excavator/claude-erasmus-2026-11-02/r2/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-erasmus-2026-11-02/r2/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW.jsonl","pointer":"line:3","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"9fea503fcb6a0a237442acdd1a35cec14b467e7bcf22422f2e5da8fa80c3b76f","path":"research/excavator/claude-erasmus-2026-11-02/r2/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW.jsonl","pointer":"line:3","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"}],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:10138#whole"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:10138#whole"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"6361bdc557b6acaeae6e6908cded18f4f8fef9fde1a97cc11fb7c12c8cdea761","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt","sha256":"6361bdc557b6acaeae6e6908cded18f4f8fef9fde1a97cc11fb7c12c8cdea761","state":"match"},"sha256":"945348afbba863ae7dc1fbe7df8759682fe1733962734a9255a1062c0561048c","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt","text_sha256":"6361bdc557b6acaeae6e6908cded18f4f8fef9fde1a97cc11fb7c12c8cdea761"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"f64f31b0e582fe272db8ed610f168749f479c4dc274e57cd0cdfa47c40df1d15","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10138.txt","sha256":"f64f31b0e582fe272db8ed610f168749f479c4dc274e57cd0cdfa47c40df1d15","state":"match"},"sha256":"a55ca3dd83cad5db6e88c0fec3b07fc70ab8f8e415f7088acc756540769c37b0","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10138.txt","text_sha256":"f64f31b0e582fe272db8ed610f168749f479c4dc274e57cd0cdfa47c40df1d15"}]}]}

the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10139 at 15 FR 4241, in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads FEDERAL REGISTER 4241 with the date Tuesday, July 4, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10139 and is signed July 3, 1950. Its filing line in the text layer reads Filed, July 8, 1950, which cannot be right for a page published on July 4, 1950 and is read as an OCR error for July 3. The same page also prints Executive Order 10138, which concerns the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, Local 158, A. F. of L.; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it states \"I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute.\" It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President \"within thirty days from the date of this order\", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported \"no change, except by agreement, shall be made\" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed \"Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986\" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that \"the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked\"; its No. Subject table lists 10139 with the subject \"Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute\". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10139_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10139_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_fe19979d2d.txt, PDF page 1) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed July 3, 1950 by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139, and its title page is dated at Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10136 to 10139 hold the same pages) and a Federal Register codification guide for page 4241.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report requirement is a deadline, not an end. (2) The thirty-day period after the report during which no change could be made except by agreement comes from section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the held sources do not show when the President received the report, so no exact end of that period is asserted, and its running out is a spent fact, not an end. (3) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation, and the held-text number search found no other instrument naming the order. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order has no command independent of the board it creates. The bar on interested members, the thirty-day report command and the sentence on unchanged conditions all serve the same board and share the order's end. The board's investigation, its report and any settlement that followed are completed past events, not continuing commands of this order; the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives it, and no held source shows any continuing effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, its table row matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so it reaches the whole order. the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10140 (15 FR 4333; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10140 and signed July 6, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pullman Company and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10140 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.\",\"savings_check\":\"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10142 (15 FR 4465; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10142 and signed July 12, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Braniff Airways, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway & Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10142 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. Order 10147 and signed August 4, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the New York Central Railroad Company, Lines East of Buffalo, and certain of its employees represented by four railroad labor organizations, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10147 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by any of the carriers involved or their employees in the conditions out of which the said disputes arose.

Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Atlantic & East Carolina Railway Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the sixteen cooperating non-operating labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that each carrier involved be given independent consideration and that the labor organizations be permitted to function as a unit before the board; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Lists A and B (the carriers and the labor organizations) follow the signature block in the held text; they identify the parties and are not separate commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, \"it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and\" and, on the next line, \"any amendments thereto, are revoked:\" (the table row for 10150 describes creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking September 9, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on September 9, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to October 9, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10165 (15 FR 6737; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10165 and signed October 3, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Locals 808 and 459, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10165 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.\",\"savings_check\":\"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the American Airlines, Inc., or its employees in the conditions out of which the said dispute arose.

the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10203 (16 FR 385; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10203 and signed January 13, 1951. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the American Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10203 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.\",\"savings_check\":\"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[{"file_sha256":"6b067cb2b9d1ca895a51a7fa83f715f8f67dde108b6d8ee7dfd009452b533611","path":"research/excavator/claude-apollo-2026-10-31/g04/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-apollo-2026-10-31/g04/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW.jsonl","pointer":"line:15","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"6b067cb2b9d1ca895a51a7fa83f715f8f67dde108b6d8ee7dfd009452b533611","path":"research/excavator/claude-apollo-2026-10-31/g04/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW.jsonl","pointer":"line:15","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"}],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:10203#whole"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:10203#whole"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"6361bdc557b6acaeae6e6908cded18f4f8fef9fde1a97cc11fb7c12c8cdea761","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt","sha256":"6361bdc557b6acaeae6e6908cded18f4f8fef9fde1a97cc11fb7c12c8cdea761","state":"match"},"sha256":"945348afbba863ae7dc1fbe7df8759682fe1733962734a9255a1062c0561048c","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt","text_sha256":"6361bdc557b6acaeae6e6908cded18f4f8fef9fde1a97cc11fb7c12c8cdea761"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"74d28d095e5b6aa15782d25c95969f28634590c69d72bb958cb590cc6abce4bd","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10203.txt","sha256":"74d28d095e5b6aa15782d25c95969f28634590c69d72bb958cb590cc6abce4bd","state":"match"},"sha256":"8e6f0495b07521d95a0846476c0631aab3745516f210a69b59b79e642c6be905","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10203.txt","text_sha256":"74d28d095e5b6aa15782d25c95969f28634590c69d72bb958cb590cc6abce4bd"}]}]}

Washington, Tuesday, August 29, 1950
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10155
P ossession , C ontrol , and  O peration  of
Certain  R ailroads
WHEREAS I  find that as a result of
labor'disturbances there are interrup­
tions, and threatened interruptions, of
the operations of the transportation sys­
tems owned or operated by the carriers
by railroad named in the list attached
hereto and made a part hereof; that it
has become necessary to take possession
and assume control of the said trans­
portation systems for purposes that are
needful or desirable in connection with
the present emergency; and that the
exercise, as hereinafter specified, of the
powers vested in me is necessary to in­
sure in the national interest the opera­
tion of the said transportation systems:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the
power and authority vested in me by the
Constitution and the laws of the United
States, including the act of August 29,
1916, 39 Stat. 619, 645, as President of
the United States and as Commander in
Chief of the armed forces of the United
States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1 . Possession, control, and operation of
the transportation systems owned or op­
erated by the carriers by railroad named
in the list attached hereto and hereby
made a part hereof are hereby taken
and assumed, through the Secretary of
the Army (hereinafter referred to as the
Secretary), as of 4 o’clock P. M. Eastern
Standard Time, August 27, 1950; but
such possession and control shall be lim­
ited to real and personal property and
other assets used or useful in connection
with the operation of the transportation
systems of the said carriers. If and
when the Secretary finds it necessary or
appropriate for carrying out the pur­
poses of this order, he may, by appro­
priate order, take possession and assume
control of all or any part of any trans­
portation system of any other carrier by
railroad located in the continental
United States.
2. The Secretary is directed to operate,
or to arrange for the operation of, the
transportation systems taken under, or
which may be taken pursuant to, this
order in such manner as he deems neces­
sary to assure to the fullest possible ex­
tent continuous and uninterrupted
transportation service.
3. In carrying out the provisions of
this order the Secretary may act through
or with the aid of such public or private
instrumentalities or persons as he may
designate, and may delegate such of his
authority as he may deem necessary or
desirable. The Secretary may issue such
general and special orders, rules, and
regulations as may be necessary or ap­
propriate for carrying out the provisions,
and to accomplish the purposes, of this
order. All Federal agencies shall com­
ply with the orders of the Secretary is­
sued pursuant to this order and shall
cooperate to the fullest extent of their
authority with the Secretary in carry­
ing out the provisions of this order.
4. The Secretary shall permit the
management of carriers whose transpor­
tation systems have been taken under, or
which may be taken pursuant to, the
provisions of this order to continue their
respective managerial functions to the
maximum degree possible consistent with
the purposes of this order. Except so
far as the Secretary shall from time to
time otherwise provide by appropriate
order or regulation, the boards of direc­
tors, trustees, receivers, officers, and em­
ployees of such carriers shall continue
the operation of the said transportation
systems, including the collection and dis­
bursement of funds thereof, in the usual
and ordinary course of the business of
the carriers, in the names of their re­
spective companies, and by means of any
agencies, associations, or other instru­
mentalities now utilized by the carriers.
5. Except so far as the Secretary shall
from time to time otherwise determine
and provide by appropriate orders or
regulations, existing contracts and
agreements to which carriers whose
transportation systems have been taken
under, or which may be taken pursuant
to, the provisions of this order are par­
ties, shall remain in full force and effect.
Nothing in this order shall have the
effect of suspending or releasing any ob­
ligation owed to any carrier affected
hereby, and all payments shall be made
by the perspns obligated to the carrier
to which they are or may become due.
Except as the Secretary may otherwise
direct, there may be made, in due course,

6. Until further order of the President
or the Secretary, the said transportation
systems shall be managed and operated
under the terms and conditions of em­
ployment in effect on August 20, 1950,
without prejudice to existing equities or
to the effectiveness of such retroactive
provisions as may be included in the
final settlement of the disputes between
the carriers and the workers. The Sec­
retary shall recognize the right of the
workers to continue their membership in
labor organizations, to bargain collec­
tively through representatives of their
own choosing with the representatives
of the owners of the carriers, subject to
the provisions of applicable law, as to
disputes between the carriers and the
workers; and to engage in concerted
activities for the purpose of such col­
lective bargaining or for other mutual
aid or protection, provided that in his
opinion such concerted activities do not
interfere with the operation of the
transportation systems taken hereunder,
or which may be taken pursuant hereto.
7. Except as this order otherwise pro­
vides and except as the Secretary may
otherwise direct, the operation of the
transportation systems taken hereunder,
or which may be taken pursuant hereto,
shall be in conformity with the Inter­
state Commerce Act, as amended, the
FEDERAL REGISTER
Railway Labor Act, as amended, the
Safety Appliance Acts, the Employers'
Liability Acts, and other applicable Fed­
eral and State laws, Executive orders,
local ordinances, and rules and regula­
tions issued pursuant to such laws,
Executive orders, and ordinances.
8. Except with the prior written con­
sent of the Secretary, no receivership,
reorganization, or similar proceeding
affecting any carrier whose transporta­
tion system is taken hereunder, or which
may be taken pursuant hereto, shall be
instituted; and no attachment by mesne
process, garnishment, execution, or
otherwise shall be levied on or against
any of the real or personal property or
other assets of any such carrier; pro­
vided that nothing herein shall prevent
or require approval by the Secretary of
any action authorized or required by any
interlocutory or final decree of any
United States court in reorganization
proceedings how pending under the
Bankruptcy Act or in any equity re­
ceivership cases now pending.
9. The Secretary is authorized to fur­
nish protection for persons employed or
seeking employment in or with the
transportation systems of which posses-
sion is taken hereunder, or which may
be taken pursuant hereto; to furnish
protection for such transportation sys­
tems; and to furnish equipment, man­
power, and other facilities or services
deemed necessary to carry out the provi­
sions and to accomplish the purposes of
this order.
10. From And after 4 o’clock P. M.,
Eastern Standard Time, on the said 27th
day of August, 1950, all properties taken
under, or which may be taken pursuant
to, this order shall be conclusively
deemed to be within the possession and
control of the United .States without
further act or notice.
11. Possession, control, and operation
of any transportation system, or any part
thereof, or of any real or personal prop­
erty taken under, or which may be taken
pursuant to, this order shall be termi­
nated by the Secretary when he deter-'
mines that such possession, control, and
operation are no longer necessary to
carry out the provisions and to accom­
plish the purposes of this order.

D esignatio n  of C ertain  O fficers  of th e
D epartment  of  the  I nterior  T o A ct as
S ecretary  of  the  I nterior
By virtue of the authority vested in
me by section 179 of the Revised Statutes
of the United States (5 U. S. C. 6), and as
President of the United States, it is
ordered as follows:
1 . (a) The Under Secretary of the In­
terior shall perform the duties of the
Secretary of the Interior in case of the
death, resignation, absence, or sickness
of the Secretary of the Interior.
(b) The ranking Assistant Secretary
of the Interior present shall perform the
duties of the Secretary of the Interior in
case of the death, resignation, absence,
or sickness of both the Secretary of the
Interior and the Under Secretary of the
Interior.
(c) The Solicitor of the Department
of the Interior shall perform the duties
of the Secretary of the Interior in case
of the death, resignation, absence, or
sickness of the Secretary, the Under Sec­
retary, and the Assistant Secretaries of
the Interior.
2. The Assistant Secretary of the
Interior whose commission bears the
earliest date, or, if the commissions of
Assistant Secretaries bear the same date,
the Assistant Secretary who first took the
oath of office, shall be considered the
ranking Assistant Secretary of the In­
terior for the purposes of paragraph 1
(b) of this order.
3. This order supersedes Executive
Order No. 98661  of June 14,1947, entitled
“Designation of Officers To Act as Secre­
tary of the Interior.”

REQUIREMENTS FOR 1950
Basis and purpose.  The revised de­
termination set forth below is made pur­
suant to section 201 of the Sugar Act
of 1948« The act requires that the Sec­
retary shall revise the determination of
sugar requirements at such times during
the calendar year as may be necessary.
It now appears that an increase in the
estimate of requirements for the cal­
endar year 1950 is necessary. The pur­
pose of this revision is to make such
determination conform to the require­
ments indicated on the basis of the fac­
tors specified in section 201 of the act.
Immediate availability of a part of the
additional supply of sugar provided by
this determination of sugar requirements
is necessary to insure orderly marketing
and to maintain a continuous and stable
supply of sugar at prices that are not
excessive to consumers. Therefore, in
order effectively to carry out the pur­
poses of the Sugar Act, It is necessary
that the revision of the determination be
made effective as soon as possible. Ac­
cordingly, it is hereby determined and
found that compliance with the notice,
procedure, and effective date require­
ments of the Administrative Procedure
Act (60 Stat. 237; 5 U. S. C. 1001) is im­
practicable and contrary to the public
interest, and the revision of the deter­
mination made herein shall be effective
on the date of its publication in the
F ederal  R egister .
By virtue of the authority vested in
the Secretary of Agriculture by the
Sugar Act of 1948 (61 Stat. 922, 7 U. S. C.,
Supp. I, 1100) and the Administrative
Procedure Act (60 Stat. 237, 5 U. S. C.

the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10285 at 16 FR 9135, in the Federal Register of September 8, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10285 and is signed September 6, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between The Denver & Rio Grande Western Railroad Company, including the Denver & Salt Lake Railroad Company, a carrier under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, and recites that by Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950 the President, through the Secretary of the Army, assumed possession, control and operation of the carrier's transportation system. Invoking the Constitution and laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, and subject to that section, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its operative text then has three more sentences: \"Nothing in this order shall be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under the said Executive Order No. 10155.\"; a sentence directing the board to \"report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order\" (the text layer drops the sentence's first word); and \"In performing its functions under this order the Board shall comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended.\" Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the Defense Production Act sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed \"Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986\" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that \"the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked\"; its No. Subject table lists 10285 with the subject \"Creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain workers and a railroad operated by the Secretary of the Army\". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10285_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10285_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ec5eddd465.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board created September 6, 1951 by Executive Order 10285, and its title page and letter of transmittal are dated at Denver, September 19, 1951. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 10155. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10285, 10286 and 10287) and the front matter of the board's report.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report requirement is a deadline, not an end. The board's held report is dated September 19, 1951; that date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The order acts subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; any period that statute fixes after the report is the statute's own effect and a spent fact, not an end of the order. (3) The Defense Production Act sentence governs how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, and the board's functions ended in practice with its report, so no expiry of that statute is claimed as an end. (4) Executive Order 10155 is recited as the basis of federal operation and in the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority; it predates this order and does not act on it. (5) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation and the cross-reference to Executive Order 10155. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order's operative text has four elements: the creation of the board subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority under Executive Order 10155, the thirty-day report command, and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence. None is independent of the board: the preserving sentence is a rule of construction that creates no duty of its own, and the compliance sentence is a condition on how the board works. All share the order's end.\",\"savings_check\":\"The enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 contains no saving or exception clause, and the ACT record for this pair lists none. The board's investigation, its report and any settlement that followed are completed past events, not continuing commands of this order; the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives it, and no held source shows any continuing effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, its table row matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so it reaches the whole order. The order has no amendment in the held corpus. govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10303, is signed November 6, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Nov. 7, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad Company, the Chicago & North Western Railway Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company, the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis and all other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees, carriers under Federal management, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, and recites that by Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950 the President, through the Secretary of the Army, assumed possession, control and operation of those carriers' transportation systems. Invoking the Constitution and laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, and subject to that section, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its operative text then has three more sentences: a sentence that nothing in the order shall be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155; \"The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.\"; and a sentence requiring the Board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the dossier split the order into two clauses at the number 10155, which ends the sentence on the Secretary of the Army's authority. The order has no numbered paragraphs, so the inventory is corrected to one whole-order clause from the heading through the Defense Production Act sentence. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed \"Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986\" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that \"the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked\"; its No. Subject table lists 10303 with the subject \"Creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between employees and transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army\". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10303_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10303_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_502ff45635.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board created November 6, 1951 by Executive Order 10303, and its title page is dated at Washington, D. C., January 25, 1952. The same report states that the parties obtained an extension of the time for the report after the hearings began late. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 10155. The held-text number search found this number only in the Federal Register text file of the order's own printing and the front matter of the board's report.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report requirement is a deadline, not an end. The board's held report bears the date January 25, 1952 on its title page; that date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The order acts subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; any period that statute fixes after the report is the statute's own effect and a spent fact, not an end of the order. (3) The Defense Production Act sentence governs how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, and the board's functions ended in practice with its report, so no expiry of that statute is claimed as an end. (4) Executive Order 10155 is recited as the basis of federal operation and in the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority; it predates this order and does not act on it. (5) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation and the cross-reference to Executive Order 10155. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order's operative text has four elements: the creation of the board subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority under Executive Order 10155, the thirty-day report command, and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence. None is independent of the board: the preserving sentence is a rule of construction that creates no duty of its own, and the compliance sentence is a condition on how the board works. All share the order's end.\",\"savings_check\":\"The enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 contains no saving or exception clause, and the ACT record for this pair lists none. The board's investigation, its report and any settlement that followed are completed past events, not continuing commands of this order; the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives it, and no held source shows any continuing effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, its table row matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so it reaches the whole order. The order has no amendment in the held corpus. the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10303 (16 FR 11321; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10303 and signed November 6, 1951. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (subject to that section) to investigate the dispute between certain transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order, a sentence that nothing in the order derogates from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order 10155 of August 25, 1950, and a sentence requiring the Board to comply with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline, the non-derogation sentence and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10303 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between employees and transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed. The sentence requiring compliance with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, so no expiry of that statute is shown and none is claimed as an earlier end. Executive Order 10155 of August 25, 1950 is recited as background and as a non-derogation reference; it predates this order and is not an actor affecting it.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute. The Defense Production Act compliance sentence is a condition on the board's performance, not a separate command with its own sunset shown in held evidence. The non-derogation sentence is a rule of construction preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority under EO 10155; it creates no separate duty.\",\"savings_check\":\"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.\",\"scope_check\":\"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 3795 to 6308 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, carriers under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the seventeen cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order, and that the President had assumed possession, control and operation of the carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950. Acting under the Constitution and the laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; states that nothing in the order is to be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 (the order under which the President had assumed possession of these carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army); it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and directs that, in performing its functions under the order, the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. It contains no sentence imposing a status-quo standstill on the carriers or employees. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, \"it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and\" and, on the next line, \"any amendments thereto, are revoked:\" (the table row for 10306 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking February 14, 1952 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on February 14, 1952 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to March 15, 1952 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation.
